question: Supporting generational renewal and small family farms under the post-2027 CAP

Generational renewal is one of the biggest challenges that European agriculture is facing. The Commission’s proposal for the post-2027 CAP provides for specific forms of support for young farmers and small holdings – including potential annual lump-sum payments of up to EUR 3 000 for small farmers as well as start-up aid, vocational training and skill development measures.

Romania’s current system provides for redistributive aid and additional income support for young farmers who meet specific eligibility criteria. Under the new framework, income support instruments would come under the broader remit of national and regional partnership plans. 1.

How will the Commission ensure that the integration of the current CAP instruments into the new framework does not reduce the actual support made available to young farmers and small family-owned holdings in Romania?

Does the Commission intend to set measurable targets and monitoring indicators for generational renewal to, among other things, keep tabs on how many young farmers are being supported and assess the viability of newly established farms and their access to farmland and investment funding?

What safeguards will be in place to ensure that support for small farms, including the proposed annual lump-sum payment capped at EUR 3 000, remains accessible to eligible Romanian farmers and is ring-fenced from any changes in the NRPP’s budgetary priorities?
